title: HF pressure sensors
scope: Generic class mechanism in representative anatomy. The anatomy, device shape and positions shown are representative of this class; they are not measured on a specific patient or population, and not a specific product. Schematic, not to scale; poses do not predict clinical fit, deformation, performance or flow.
stageLabel: Schematic · representative anatomy · not to scale
attribution: Whole-heart context adapted from Toronto Heart Atlas by Azad Mashari, Joshua Qua Hiansen, Mini Pakkal, Eitan Aziza, Ryan Ramos, Sachin Khargie and Massimiliano Meineri (CC BY 4.0). Display smoothing, vessel continuations and edits for readability are modifications. Detailed tissue shells, defects, device shapes and positions are representative schematics. They are not measured on a specific patient or population, and are not segmented tissue or clinical simulations.

designs.summary: A small sensing body with soft anchoring loops, illustrated in a branch pulmonary artery.

views.label: Whole heart
views.title: Locate the treatment region
views.lesson: Use the highlighted region to orient the enlarged views.

views.label: Pulmonary artery branches
views.title: Locate the sensor beyond the pulmonary trunk
views.lesson: Seen from the left and above, the pulmonary trunk rises from the right ventricle and divides into the left and right pulmonary arteries. The near wall of the trunk and left branch is cut away. The vessels come from a real heart model with walls added. The sensor's position in the left branch is representative and is not measured on a specific patient or population.

views.label: Mechanism section
views.title: See the tissue–device relationship
views.lesson: The body stays small relative to the illustrated lumen; compare how the anchoring loops change shape.

views.label: Oblique detail
views.title: Understand depth and attachment
views.lesson: An oblique view separates the near surface, device and supporting tissue.

views.label: Face view
views.title: Look along the opening
views.lesson: The face view complements the section. All poses and proportions are representative, not measured.

location.label: TREATMENT LOCATION
location.body: The highlighted region locates this class in the heart. The marker is enlarged for orientation.

wall.label: BRANCH PULMONARY ARTERY
wall.body: The open wall is a representative section of an artery. Its lumen remains visible around the sensor.

body.label: SENSING BODY
body.body: The generic capsule identifies the sensing element; electronics and calibration are not represented.

anchor.label: ANCHORING LOOPS
anchor.body: Loops change from compact to expanded representative poses. They illustrate retention without predicting wall force.

region_trunk.label: PULMONARY TRUNK
region_trunk.body: The main pulmonary artery leaves the right ventricle through the pulmonary valve opening and rises toward its branches.

region_branch.label: RIGHT PULMONARY ARTERY
region_branch.body: The right branch runs behind the aorta toward the right lung. It gives context for the branch that holds the sensor.

region_target.label: LEFT PULMONARY ARTERY
region_target.body: The left branch arches backward toward the left lung. In this example the sensor sits in it, beyond the division of the trunk.

region_RV.label: RIGHT VENTRICLE
region_RV.body: The right ventricle pumps into the pulmonary trunk. It is shown for orientation.

region_body.label: SENSING BODY
region_body.body: The generic capsule lies along the branch, with blood flowing past it. Its position is representative.

region_anchor.label: ANCHORING LOOPS
region_anchor.body: The loops change from compact to expanded poses and rest against the branch wall. They illustrate retention without predicting wall force.
